newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS - edging lower after last wk's drop.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS - edging lower after last wk's drop.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds in early trade on Monday were seen from flat to down about 1/4 point, as the market looked for a bottom after last week's dive.
"There probably hasn't been a trade yet...We're hoping for a bounce," a trader said.

With fairly few economic reports due out this week, municipal bonds were expected to concentrate on new issues, which were expected to total $3.9 billion in 111 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings totalled $2.8 billion in 49 sales, with a $464 million Allegheny County Airport, Pa., sale through Morgan Stanley & Co Inc topping the list.

The market's eye also was drawn to an approximately $365 million sale of bonds by the New York City Water Finance Authority, which only attracted $4 million of retail orders on Friday, the first day of the preorder period, due to the big drop in fixed income markets.

There was speculation that the bonds would be repriced on Monday morning with higher yields for individual investors. A New York City official was not immediately available to comment. Both Standard and Poor's Corp and Moody's Investors Service have given the Authority a positive outlook.
Institutional investors will see their prices for the offering on Tuesday morning.
On the competitive side, 62 sales totaling $1.1 billion were scheduled. A $240 million Georgia offering on Tuesday was the largest.
At 1000 EDT, the Commerce Department was scheduled to release construction spending, which was expected to have climbed 1.1 percent, a turnaround from the previous month's drop of 1.8 percent.

In early activity in Chicago, September municipal futures fell six ticks to 120-10/32, while September Treasury futures also slipped six ticks to 114-20/32. This left the MOB spread between the two futures contracts at plus 182 ticks, unchanged from higher levels seen late Friday, when municipal bonds did not fall as steeply as Treasuries.
In the secondary market, Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority bonds of 2024, which pay a 5.0 percent coupon, were bid at 5.45 percent, NET, up three basis points.
And Municipal Electricity Authority of Georgia bonds of 2026, which carry a 5.0 percent coupon, were offered at 5.30 percent, NET, unchanged.
